blueprint_concepts: Family of lines through the intersection of two lines

concept_use.Family of lines through the intersection: L_lambda is the family of lines through the intersection (1,-2) of 2x - y - 4 = 0 and x + y + 1 = 0; this fixes when L_lambda meets Gamma and when it passes through O.
concept_use.Family of circles: C_lambda is written as the family of circles Gamma + t L_lambda = 0 through the chord's end points, and regrouping by lambda gives the fixed point.

english: Let $\Gamma$ be the circle $x^2+y^2=25$. For a real number $\lambda$, let $L_\lambda$ be the line $(2x-y-4)+\lambda(x+y+1)=0$. For every $\lambda$ for which $L_\lambda$ does not pass through the origin $O$, let $C_\lambda$ be the circle passing through $O$ and through the two points where $L_\lambda$ meets $\Gamma$. All the circles $C_\lambda$ pass through a fixed point $(\alpha,\beta)$ different from $O$. Then the value of $\alpha+\beta$ is ______.
hindi: माना $\Gamma$ वृत्त $x^2+y^2=25$ है। एक वास्तविक संख्या $\lambda$ के लिए, माना $L_\lambda$ रेखा $(2x-y-4)+\lambda(x+y+1)=0$ है। $\lambda$ के प्रत्येक ऐसे मान के लिए जिसके लिए $L_\lambda$ मूल बिन्दु $O$ से होकर नहीं जाती, माना $C_\lambda$ वह वृत्त है जो $O$ से तथा उन दो बिन्दुओं से होकर जाता है जहाँ $L_\lambda$, $\Gamma$ से मिलती है। सभी वृत्त $C_\lambda$, $O$ से भिन्न एक स्थिर बिन्दु $(\alpha,\beta)$ से होकर जाते हैं। तब $\alpha+\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $L_\lambda$ passes through $2x-y-4=0\cap x+y+1=0=(1,-2)$, inside $\Gamma$; it passes through $O$ only for $\lambda=4$
solution_full: Every $L_\lambda$ passes through the intersection of $2x-y-4=0$ and $x+y+1=0$: adding, $3x-3=0$, so the point is $(1,-2)$. It lies inside $\Gamma$ ($1+4<25$), so each $L_\lambda$ meets $\Gamma$ in two points. $L_\lambda$ passes through $O$ when $-4+\lambda=0$, i.e. $\lambda=4$, which is excluded.

The circles through the two points common to $\Gamma$ and $L_\lambda$ are $x^2+y^2-25+t\left[(2+\lambda)x+(\lambda-1)y+(\lambda-4)\right]=0$. Passing through $O$: $-25+t(\lambda-4)=0$, so $t=\dfrac{25}{\lambda-4}$.

Multiplying by $(\lambda-4)$: $(\lambda-4)(x^2+y^2-25)+25\left[(2+\lambda)x+(\lambda-1)y+(\lambda-4)\right]=0$, which simplifies (the constants cancel) to $\lambda\left(x^2+y^2+25x+25y\right)+\left(-4x^2-4y^2+50x-25y\right)=0$.
So every $C_\lambda$ belongs to the family of circles through the common points of $x^2+y^2+25x+25y=0$ and $4x^2+4y^2-50x+25y=0$, and a point lies on all $C_\lambda$ exactly when it lies on both.
Subtracting the second from $4$ times the first: $150x+75y=0$, so $y=-2x$. Then $x^2+4x^2+25x-50x=0\Rightarrow5x(x-5)=0$.
Check by power of a point: $(1,-2)$ has power $1+4-25=-20$ with respect to $\Gamma$; on the ray from $O$ through $(1,-2)$ the point $R$ with $PO\cdot PR=20$ is $(1,-2)+4(1,-2)=(5,-10)$.
originality_note: New: two families are nested (a pencil of lines through a point and, for each line, the circle through its chord of a fixed circle and the origin), and the hidden invariant is a second fixed point common to all these circles (way 4). Closest known: 'family of lines through the intersection of two lines' and 'family of circles S + t L = 0'. Different because: neither family alone answers the question; eliminating the line parameter shows the circles form a coaxal family through a fixed point.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, curve and symbol is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath (and a numerical brute-force check), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Excluded the one line through O (lambda = 4), for which the circle does not exist. Changed: added the exclusion.
key_step: Writing C_lambda = Gamma + t L_lambda through O and regrouping by lambda to find the two base circles of the family.
justification: Two family ideas combined and a fixed point found by eliminating the parameter; numerical answer. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q13 (L4) in idea type but lighter, so L3.
